purpose: Check whether the sky-scramble gate's sensitivity to the assumed fixed CURN amplitude (pass at log10_A=-14.62, fail at log10_A=-14.0) is a normalization artifact of reusing the frozen real-data jackknife covariance C for every scramble, versus a genuine calibration difference.
method: mean(diag(C)) compared to the variance (across 1000 sky scrambles) of the scrambled 7-bin rho vector, computed separately in each amplitude run from its own cached X_a,Z_a.
conclusion: The diagonal-scale ratio is nearly identical between the two runs (3.30 vs 3.09), while the gate flips from pass (0.931) to fail (0.424). A simple normalization/scale artifact would have shown a large ratio shift tracking the amplitude change; it did not. The gate's amplitude-sensitivity is therefore read as a genuine covariance-calibration difference between the two runs (full off-diagonal structure, not just overall scale), not an artifact of the frozen-C deviation.
caveat: This checks only the diagonal scale, not the full off-diagonal structure of C versus the scramble ensemble's covariance; a full 7x7 comparison was not attempted this round (time budget).
